failureMessage: a token whose header claims alg "none" carries no signature at all, so a verifier that accepts it treats attacker-written claims as authenticated — the classic signature-stripping bypass

matchLines.what: lists "none" in a JWT verification-algorithm allowlist
matchLines.fix: remove "none" — an unsigned token must never verify; list only the exact algorithm(s) this verifier expects

failureMessage: without an allowlist the verification algorithm comes from the token's own header — the attacker writes that header, so they pick the algorithm

matchLines.what: verifies a JWT with no algorithms allowlist (and none is set anywhere in this file)
matchLines.fix: pass { algorithms: ['<the one algorithm this issuer uses>'] } to every jsonwebtoken verify call — never let the token pick

failureMessage: the signature proves who signed the token, not who it was for — without an audience/issuer check, a valid token minted for a different service or purpose is accepted here (substitution attack)

matchLines.what: verifies a JWT binding neither audience nor issuer (neither word appears in this file)
matchLines.fix: pass the expected audience (and issuer) to the verify call so a token minted for another recipient is rejected — validate every claim the token carries
